newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures firm more late, end near highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures firm more late, end near highs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures firmed again late and ended pit trade flirting with session highs.
December Treasury bond futures pushed higher into the closing bell on what traders said looked like local shortcovering that triggered buy stops.
"The locals ran buy stops," said one floor broker in T-bond futures. "We had a flurry of shorts in the market getting out."
The late push tugged December T-bonds above 111-00, a level that had formed a psychological and technical barrier to recent upside attempts.
"It was a constructive close," said another floor broker. "Now we've got to see if we get some followthrough."

Futures had drifted inside tight afternoon ranges but never peeked back below the 110-28/32 level that, bracketed by Wednesday's high at 110-27/32 and Tuesday's peak at 110-29/32, had repelled buyers earlier in the week.
A slew of U.S. economic reports on Thursday, most of which showed some economic softness, helped propel futures upward.
December T-bonds initially jumped 111-00 after economically flaccid weekly jobless claims, September housing starts, industrial output and capacity use data.

The housing starts and industrial production figures show the economy losing steam while the low capacity use data suggest that price pressures to due manufacturing bottlenecks are not a threat, noted Brian Wesbury, chief economist at Griffin, Kubik, Stephens & Thompson Inc, in daily commentary.
"As a result, the Federal Reserve will leave rates unchanged for the remainder of this year and will probably move to lower interest rates early in 1997," he wrote.
Additional support came from the unexpectedly big drop in the October Philadelphia Federal Reserve index, although gains in prices helped offset the impact, brokers said.
Some brokers said futures were concerned briefly by the weakening in overseas debt markets after Russian president Boris Yeltsin sacked his security chief, Alexander Lebed.
That news sent the U.S. dollar romping even higher against the mark, but U.S. T-bond futures traders said the downward impact in their pits was shallow and shortlived.
Comments by Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey also lacked impact, brokers said.
Lindsey said after midday that he was happy with the current state of the U.S. economy and that the economy can grow faster than it has.
Friday's economic data consists of the August U.S. trade balance report, expected to show the deficit shrank to $8.5 billion from July's original $11.68 billion shortfall.

At settlement, December T-bonds were up 26/32 at 111-04/32, T-notes gained 13/32 to 108-19/32, muni-bonds added 18/32 to 114-26/32, March Eurodollars rose five basis points to 94.32, and March T-bills added six basis points to 94.85. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
